interpretation: The modal-tuple result is an optimistic in-sample diagnostic, not held-out performance.
A deterministic exact-tuple lookup maximizes in-sample accuracy by choosing each tuple's modal label, but then recovers very few partial cases.
More than 94% of partial cases share their entire score representation with an outer-class case, so improving partial recall from these scores necessarily creates many false partial predictions.
The same score representation has different label semantics across datasets. Dataset-specific score-pattern calibration is therefore unlikely to generalize.
decision: Stop adding downstream functions of the three aggregate scores. Test whether a one-call rubric can preserve condition-level achieved and missing evidence before calibration.
